recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source change is needed for FHIR-46763; the existing wording satisfies the issue without duplicating _include/_revinclude details elsewhere.
issue_request: FHIR-46763 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for R6 asking the search page to clarify that _maxresults limits returned match resources, not resources returned through _include or _revinclude. The approved resolution was to update the documentation so this extension refers only to matches and does not cover included resources or operation outcomes.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by commit 647d1548bcf7a7a6c7cdccb4a6986aad39d3718f, titled "FHIR-46763 - clarify that _maxresults only applies to matches", merged through HL7/fhir#3442. That commit added the current paragraph to source/search.html stating that _maxresults only affects resources returned as matches and does not affect included resources or operation outcomes. The combined branch already contained that implementation commit, but did not yet contain an Issue-Reconcile-Key audit commit for FHIR-46763.
additional_context: The initiating Zulip thread confirms the reporter's concern that the old wording could be read to count included resources, and Josh Mandel clarified that the intent was to limit search results rather than all response resources. FHIR-I minutes from 2024-09-09 record the 13-0-0 Persuasive motion to update documentation that _maxresults is for matches. Current source/search.html is the search page named by the Jira related URL, and the current wording expresses the approved rule using entry.search.mode=match and entry.search.mode=include.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/search.html already says _maxresults has no impact on Bundle.total, only affects resources returned as matches, and does not affect included resources or operation outcomes.
